subject: Post-incident evidence: retain/slice/escrow transfer plan and timelines
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence preservation request and scope questions

Diego —

Thanks for taking this. We completed an initial triage for the authentication anomaly that affected a small subset of production tokens last night. Acme's incident response team needs a short, concrete plan from Redwood for: (1) what logs you will preserve, (2) how you'll slice or redact PII, (3) how long preserved artifacts will be retained, and (4) the expected handoff timeline/format if we request a forensic export. We need to confirm a custody chain and ensure exports are encrypted and signed.

High-level details that would help immediately:
- Retention windows you typically apply for raw request/response payloads, access logs, and KV-cache traces in a post-incident hold.
- Whether you can produce an exported evidence bundle with a manifest and hash list for chain-of-custody.
- Your standard SLA for producing that bundle (hours/days).

We are preparing an internal evidence-hold and would like Redwood to put an explicit hold on the requested artifacts in us-west-2. Please include contact details for the engineer who will own the export.

Oliver
Incident Response Lead
Acme Health

---
Attachment: incident-reference-ACM-20280520.txt (text summary)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence preservation request and scope questions

Oliver — thanks for the clear ask. Putting Acme on a post-incident hold for the requested artifacts in us-west-2 now. Below is an actionable plan and expected timelines. Marissa and Soojin are copied for compliance and legal confirmation.

What we will preserve (initial scope):
- Raw request/response payloads (full body) for all requests matching Acme tenant IDs and the affected token set — retention hold: 365 days by default pending your direction.
- Inference traces/KV-cache snapshots used during the window — retained for 180 days unless Acme requests longer. These are large; we will provide a sliced export (see below).
- Access and control-plane logs (auth events, model routing decisions, job scheduling) — retained for 540 days for forensic completeness.
- Aggregated telemetry and anonymized traces (used for debugging) — retained 90 days.

Slicing/redaction approach:
- We can produce both (A) raw artifacts in an encrypted export and (B) a redacted export with PII removed. Redaction rules: replace any user-identifiable token artifacts with deterministic pseudonyms and retain an internal mapping in our secure KMS-wrapped store if needed for legal review.
- For KV-cache snapshots we will only export keys/values that reference Acme tenant IDs; system-level keys will be excluded.

Export format and chain-of-custody:
- Export bundle: gzipped tarball containing: logs/, requests/, kv_snapshots/, manifest.json, and signature.asc.
- manifest.json will include SHA256 checksums for each file and a human-readable manifest of collection timestamps.
- We will sign the bundle with our rotation-managed key and deliver the bundle over an S3 presigned URL to an Acme-controlled bucket or via an encrypted transfer (scp over bastion) — your preference.
- Expected initial delivery SLA: 48-72 hours for a first-pass evidence bundle targeting the incident window. Full extraction for very large KV traces may take up to 7 calendar days.

Escrow / longer-term custody
- If Acme requests escrow (third-party custodian) we will generate an export and provide the signed bundle and manifest for deposit. Additional fees may apply depending on the size and storage duration.

Owner and contact:
- Primary owner: Diego Fernandez (diego_fernandez@redwood.com) — contact for export coordination.
- Technical lead (export ops): Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com).
- Compliance/legal contact: Soojin Lee (soojin_lee@redwood.com).

Attachments: retention matrix and sample chain-of-custody template attached.

I will follow up in-thread with the proposed manifest template and a short checklist you can sign to confirm scope.

Cheers,
Diego
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence preservation request and scope questions

Oliver — a couple of compliance/technical clarifications from my side:

1) Encryption and key management: All exported bundles will be encrypted with AES-256. We will wrap the encryption key with a KMS key tied to a Redwood HSM. If Acme requires key escrow or customer-managed keys, we can accommodate via a KMS exchange workflow (this will extend prep time by ~24 hours).

2) Hashing & verification: Manifest SHA256 sums are generated server-side and independently logged to our audit pipeline. We can provide the audit record timestamp if you need an extra verification checkpoint.

3) Minimal retained copy: For SOC2 purposes we usually keep one compressed archive copy in cold storage (for 12 months) before deletion unless a longer legal hold is requested. For this specific incident, holding the bundle 365 days is reasonable as a baseline; we can extend on request.

4) Redaction policy: We will perform a non-destructive redaction (create a redacted copy and keep the raw copy in a secure vault) so that legal review can still request the raw material under elevated approval.

If you confirm the preferred transfer mechanism (Acme bucket vs. Redwood-hosted presigned link), we'll start assembling the first-pass bundle.

Marissa
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 13:40:00 -07:00

Oliver — adding the legal perspective. Two quick items to expedite: 

A) Please reply with a minimal scope confirmation email (one-liner) that authorizes Redwood to: (i) create the encrypted export for the incident window, (ii) hold the exported bundle for 365 days, and (iii) provide the bundle to Acme's designated S3 bucket. That confirmation creates a clear record for us.

B) If Acme requires a notarized chain-of-custody or specific jurisdictional handling for PHI, tell us now so we can loop our privacy counsel. Without that, the standard export and manifest will suffice.

Once we have your confirmation, Diego/Marissa will initiate the export and we will provide the S3 presigned link and manifest within the SLA windows previously described.

Soojin
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
